raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Add a Prometheus counter, `vllm:kv_load_failed_requests`, that counts requests affected by failed external KV cache loads. The v1 Scheduler counts them where it already handles these failures (`_handle_invalid_blocks` and `_handle_failed_recving`), so connectors and platform plugins no longer need to work this out themselves.

## Claims

- New per-engine counter (labels `model_name`, `engine`), registered when a `kv_transfer_config` is set:
  - `vllm:kv_load_failed_requests_total`: requests affected by a failed external KV cache load, including requests that share an invalid prefix block.
- Counted under both `kv_load_failure_policy` values (`recompute`: the requests are rescheduled; `fail`: they finish with an error), and for both failure reports: block-level `invalid_block_ids` (sync and async loads) and request-level `failed_recving` (the path hybrid and multi-group models must use), without double-counting when a connector reports both for the same load.
- The numbers match the scheduler's existing KV load failure log lines ("Failing N request(s) ..." / "Recovered from KV load failure: N request(s) rescheduled ..."). The counter reuses the request total behind those lines and adds no new accounting.
- Docs: the metrics table in `docs/usage/metrics.md` is generated from `loggers.py`, so it picks up the counter. The KV Load Failure Policy section in `docs/features/nixl_connector_usage.md` now points to it.

## Validation

All tests were run on a CPU-only Linux machine (Python 3.12, `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1` editable install):

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_load_failure_recovery.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_invalid_blocks_correctness.py \
  tests/v1/metrics/test_histogram_buckets.py -q
# 39 passed
```

Broader runs on the same machine:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -q        # 281 passed
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py -q  # 19 passed
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -m cpu_test tests/v1/metrics -q           # 26 passed
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -m cpu_test tests/v1/kv_connector/unit -q # 1090 passed, 3 skipped
```

Mutation check: each of these scheduler edits makes at least one new assertion fail:
- removing the increment in `_handle_failed_recving`;
- removing the increment in `_handle_invalid_blocks`;
- removing the `already_failed_req_ids` deduplication in `_handle_invalid_blocks`;
- removing the `req_id not in self.failed_recving_kv_req_ids` check in `_handle_failed_recving`;
- removing the reset in `make_stats`.

IPC and exposition check (scratch script, not committed): a `SchedulerStats(num_kv_load_failed_reqs=3)` was encoded and decoded with `MsgpackEncoder` / `MsgpackDecoder(EngineCoreOutputs)` (the engine-core-to-frontend path), then recorded twice for engine 1. The `/metrics` text contains:

```
vllm:kv_load_failed_requests_total{engine="0",model_name="facebook/opt-125m"} 0.0
vllm:kv_load_failed_requests_total{engine="1",model_name="facebook/opt-125m"} 6.0
```

**Not run: a live end-to-end check.** The intended check is `examples/disaggregated/kv_load_failure_recovery_offline` with `LLM(disable_log_stats=False)` followed by `llm.get_metrics()`. It could not run on this machine because there is no GPU and a CPU source build requires `numa.h` (`libnuma-dev`), which is not installed; the full scheduler -> `SchedulerStats` -> `MsgpackEncoder` / `MsgpackDecoder(EngineCoreOutputs)` -> `PrometheusStatLogger.record()` -> `/metrics` pipeline was verified end-to-end above.

New or extended assertions:

| Path | Policy | Test |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `failed_recving` (alone or with `invalid_block_ids` in the same step) | fail, recompute | `test_failed_receive_completion_honors_failure_policy` (also checks the count resets after `make_stats`) |
| `invalid_block_ids` then `failed_recving` across steps (e.g. `KVOutputAggregator` under TP > 1) | fail, recompute | `test_invalid_blocks_then_failed_recving_counts_once` |
| `invalid_block_ids`, sync load | fail | `test_sync_fail_invalid_blocks_evicted` |
| `invalid_block_ids`, async load | recompute | `test_async_recompute_blocks_not_cached_when_invalid` |
| `invalid_block_ids`, shared prefix block | recompute | `test_sync_load_failure_with_shared_blocks` (both requests counted) |
| Prometheus registration and per-engine increments | n/a | `test_kv_load_failed_requests_counter` (with and without `kv_transfer_config`) |

`test_failed_receive_completion_honors_failure_policy`, `test_invalid_blocks_then_failed_recving_counts_once`, and `test_sync_load_failure_with_shared_blocks` are marked `cpu_test`. CI only runs `-m cpu_test v1/kv_connector/unit` (the GPU `v1-kv-connectors` step is commented out in `.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml`), so without the marker the new assertions would never run. All three tests pass on CPU.

`pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: all hooks pass (ruff check, ruff format, typos, markdownlint, mypy, check-test-tethering, and others).

## Details

**Why in the scheduler.** The scheduler already decides which requests a failed load affects: it truncates `num_computed_tokens`, applies the failure policy, and logs totals. A connector or platform plugin that wants this metric has to rebuild that decision from outside, for example by tracking block claims per request and retiring them across async-scheduling steps, and it still gets shared-prefix and policy cases wrong. Counting at the decision point gives one definition for every connector.

**Accounting.**
- `_handle_invalid_blocks`: adds `sync_failed_req_ids` plus `async_failed_req_ids` not already failed by `_handle_failed_recving` in the same step (so connectors like `NixlConnector` that report both `failed_recving` and `invalid_block_ids` on non-HMA models count the request once under `policy=fail`).
- `_handle_failed_recving`: adds affected `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` requests not already in `failed_recving_kv_req_ids` (so under `KVOutputAggregator` with TP > 1, where `invalid_block_ids` can arrive a step before `failed_recving`, the request is counted once under `policy=recompute`).
- A request is counted each time a distinct failure report affects it. A progressive async load that reports invalid blocks in several steps can therefore count the same request more than once, just as it produces more than one log line today.
- The count is kept on the scheduler and moved into `SchedulerStats` (then reset) in `make_stats`, the same way `connector_prefix_cache_stats` works. `make_stats` runs at the end of every `update_from_output` when stats are enabled, so nothing is lost between steps. With `log_stats=False` the integer is never read.

**Registration.** The counter is created only when `kv_transfer_config` is set. Load failures need a connector, and this follows how other optional metrics are handled: `vllm:num_requests_kv_fetch_by_stage` (KV consumers only), `vllm:watermark_requests`, and `vllm:corrupted_requests`. For the same reason it is not added to `EXPECTED_METRICS_V1` in `tests/entrypoints/serve/instrumentator/test_metrics.py`.

**No `connector` or `policy` label.** `kv_load_failure_policy` is a single engine-wide setting. Under `MultiConnector`, the scheduler only receives the merged `invalid_block_ids` and `failed_recving`, so it cannot say which child connector failed. Per-child attribution belongs in connector stats (`KVConnectorStats` / `build_prom_metrics`) and can be added later.

**Not covered here.**
- Rust frontend: `SchedulerStats` decoding in `rust/src/engine-core-client/src/protocol/stats.rs` ignores unknown fields, so the new field does not break it, but the Rust `/metrics` endpoint does not export this counter yet. It also does not export `vllm:num_requests_kv_fetch_by_stage`. This can be added in a follow-up.
- `LoggingStatLogger`: the scheduler already logs each failure at warning level (`recompute`) or error level (`fail`), so the periodic stats line is unchanged.

**Why this is not a duplicate.** Open PRs and issues searched on 2026-10-27:
- PR searches with `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search ...`: "kv load failure metric", "invalid_block_ids metric", "kv_load_failure", "failed_recving metric", "kv load failed requests", "kv load failure", "kv_load_failed", "invalid blocks metric", "kv connector metrics prometheus".
- Issue searches with `gh issue list`: "kv load failure metric", "kv load failure", "invalid_block_ids", "failed_recving", "kv_load_failure_policy metric", "kv transfer failure prometheus".

None of the results adds a failed-request counter. The closest are:
- #62685: per-request KV load wait and queue-time histograms. Different metric; it does not count failures.
- #58563: pluggable connector metrics on the Rust frontend. Connector-defined metrics; it does not count scheduler load failures.
- #63014: a warning for MultiConnector first-hit loads. Not a metric.
- #59797: KV event publisher delivery counters. Different subsystem.
- #57529 / #57530: Mooncake failure ledger. Connector-internal failure reporting, no Prometheus counter.

---

@@ -406,6 +406,8 @@ The `kv_load_failure_policy` setting controls how the system handles failures wh
 - **fail** (default): Immediately fail the request with an error when KV load fails. This prevents performance degradation by avoiding recomputation of prefill work on the decode instance.
 - **recompute**: Recompute failed blocks locally on the decode instance. This may cause performance _jitter_ on decode instances as the scheduled prefill will delay and interfere with other decodes. Furthermore, decode instances are typically configured with low-latency optimizations.
 
+Under either policy, the `vllm:kv_load_failed_requests` counter counts the requests affected by failed loads; see [Production Metrics](../usage/metrics.md).
+
 !!! warning
     Using `kv_load_failure_policy="recompute"` can lead to performance degradation in production deployments. When KV loads fail, the decode instance will execute prefill work with decode-optimized configurations, which is inefficient and defeats the purpose of disaggregated prefilling. This also increases tail latency for other ongoing decode requests.
